sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Types / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: Which part of the foot is most commonly recommended to execute an accurate short ground pass in football?
options: B) The outside of the foot
C) The inside of the foot
questions.answer: C) The inside of the foot

questions.question_text: True or False: In Kabaddi, a raider can pause to take a breath while chanting the word 'Kabaddi' as long as they are standing in their own half of the court.
questions.answer: A) True

questions.question_text: Which Yoga asana is also known as the 'Tree Pose' and greatly improves a player's neuromotor balance and focus?
questions.answer: A) Vrikshasana

questions.question_text: How many players from a single team are actively allowed on the mat at the start of a competitive Kabaddi match?
In football, what happens when a defending player intentionally touches the ball with their hands inside their own penalty box?
options: A) Throw-in for the opposing team
B) Direct free kick outside the box
C) Penalty kick awarded to the attacking team
questions.answer: C) Penalty kick awarded to the attacking team

questions.question_text: True or False: The 'Bonus Line' in Kabaddi becomes active and eligible for points only when the defending team has a minimum of 6 players on the court.
questions.answer: A) True

questions.question_text: Which Sanskrit term refers to the conscious control and regulation of breath during the practice of Yoga?
questions.answer: B) Pranayama

questions.question_text: What is the primary tactical objective of forming a 'chain tackle' in a Kabaddi match?
options: A) To run faster towards the midline
B) To trap the raider and prevent their escape
C) To score a bonus point
D) To rest during the raid
questions.answer: B) To trap the raider and prevent their escape

questions.question_text: During a standard football match, what is the maximum number of players allowed on the field for one team, excluding any substitutes on the bench?
Which fundamental seated posture in Yoga involves crossing the legs to promote deep meditation and mental calmness before a sports event?
questions.answer: A) Padmasana (Lotus Pose)

questions.question_text: Define the term 'Lona' in Kabaddi and state exactly how many bonus points are awarded for achieving it. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A 'Lona' occurs when an entire opposing team is declared out on the court. The scoring team receives two additional bonus points for this tactical achievement.

questions.question_text: Explain the correct physical technique for executing a standard push pass in football. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The player uses the inside of their foot, keeping the ankle locked and toes pointed up, striking the ball's horizontal center to ensure a flat, accurate delivery.

questions.question_text: Describe the primary physical benefit of practicing Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose) for field athletes. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Bhujangasana significantly strengthens the spinal column and stretches the chest, shoulders, and abdomen. This helps athletes improve their breathing capacity and prevents lower back injuries.

questions.question_text: Under what specific mathematical condition does a 'Super Tackle' take place for the defending team in a Kabaddi match? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A Super Tackle successfully takes place when the defending team has only three or fewer players remaining on the court and they manage to physically pin the raider.

questions.question_text: What is the main athletic objective of 'trapping' the ball in a competitive game of football? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Trapping allows a player to instantly cushion and gain complete physical control of a fast-moving ball, preparing them perfectly for an immediate pass or strike.

questions.question_text: Outline the strict physical conditions a Kabaddi raider must fulfill to successfully claim a bonus point during their raid. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: To claim a bonus point, the defending team must have at least six active players. The raider must cross the bonus line completely, keeping one foot grounded beyond it while the trailing foot remains entirely in the air.

questions.question_text: Explain how a football player effectively utilizes the instep kick technique to clear the ball long distances up the field. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The player approaches the ball at a slight angle, plants their non-kicking foot beside it, points their kicking toe down, and strikes firmly with the shoelaces (instep) to generate maximum kinetic power and an upward ball trajectory.

questions.question_text: How does the regular structural practice of Tadasana (Mountain Pose) assist students in developing better overall athletic body mechanics? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Tadasana forms the fundamental base for all standing poses. It actively corrects poor spinal alignment, improves posture, and distributes body weight evenly across both feet. This structural balance directly enhances a student's agility and stability in dynamic field sports.

questions.question_text: Describe the distinct tactical advantage of forming a 'defensive chain' instead of attempting to tackle individually in Kabaddi. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: A defensive chain involves two or more defenders holding hands to move as a single unit. This effectively minimizes gaps, blocks the raider's escape routes, and provides immediate physical support to overpower a strong raider collaboratively.

questions.question_text: Analyze how integrating specific Pranayama breathing techniques directly enhances a Kabaddi raider's performance during a continuous and aggressive raid sequence. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Pranayama systematically trains the respiratory muscles to maximize lung capacity and control oxygen flow. For a Kabaddi raider, this is crucial for sustaining a loud, unbroken 'cant' without running out of breath early. Enhanced breath management delays physical exhaustion, keeps the mind incredibly calm under pressure, and safely allows for much longer raid durations.

questions.question_text: Detail the tactical execution and spatial awareness required by a defending football team to effectively protect their goal against an incoming corner kick. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Defending a corner kick demands strict man-to-man marking or a zonal defense grid to deny attackers open space. Taller defenders position themselves centrally to intercept and head away aerial crosses. Goalkeepers must communicate loudly to command the penalty box, while edge defenders prepare to quickly clear loose balls and initiate rapid counter-attacks upon regaining possession.
